label: SEO audit broken-link findings — classification

metric.actual_meaning: broken INTERNAL links — "intl." in scripts/seo-audit.ts is an abbreviation of "internal", not "international"
metric.implementation: src/shared/audit.ts buildCockpit: counts page.internalLinks whose target starts with "/" and is absent from the set of content/pages/** URLs
metric.naming_correction: Earlier relays described these as "broken international links". The metric never had a locale dimension; the label is corrected here and the count is unchanged.

root_cause: buildCockpit builds its known-URL set from content/pages/** only. Blog articles live in content/blog/** and are prerendered separately, so every money-page -> published-article link is counted as broken. The links themselves resolve.

verification.method: each distinct flagged target was resolved against the canonical production build output

release_impact.action_taken: none — no runtime, content or route change was made
release_impact.rationale: Every finding is a metric-definition false positive: the target is a published blog article that renders at the flagged URL. There is no user-visible breakage to fix, so no content edit is justified in a security-closure sprint.

backlog.suggested_fix: Widen the known-URL set in buildCockpit to include published blog article URLs, then re-baseline the metric. That changes an audit rule and its expected counts, so it belongs to a content/SEO task, not to this closure.
